newsitem.title: CANADA: CP Rail trains delayed by West Coast storm.
newsitem.headline: CP Rail trains delayed by West Coast storm.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd railway unit CP Rail Systems on Tuesday reported continued delays due to what has been described as the worst blizzard to strike British Columbia in 75 years over the weekend.

"There have been some minor delays and that's certainly been the case in the Vancouver area where the heavy snow caused some congestion in the yards especially, but things are pretty well getting back to normal," CP Rail Systems spokesman Steve Morris said in an interview from Calgary.
Ship movements in and out of Vancouver were not hindered by the storm but CP and Canadian National trains were delayed.
"There are some minor delays to freight trains, more on the secondary or branch lines than on the main line itself," Morris said.
Canada has the third largest rail network in the world and ranks fourth worldwide in freight volume with annual revenues overall of C$7 billion.
About two feet of snow fell on the Vancouver area over the weekend.
